title: Keep internal release notes
statement: As a developer, I can keep a release's internal notes, with the tickets and details my team needs, each tied to the stories it describes or marked as a fix, so we can see exactly what went into a version.
overview: Trevor's example: the internal notes say "v0.8.1" and carry a bunch of Jira tickets. A fix can have no story; what holds the record together is that [every story in the release has code references](/requirements/every-released-story-has-code). A ticket is plain text or a URL here, with no Jira integration.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A release holds any number of internal notes, added one at a time.
A note can name outside references, such as Jira tickets, and the reader shows them with it.
Each internal note links at least one story or is marked as a fix; a note with neither is refused.
A note may only link stories the release delivers or affects; naming another is refused with the command that adds it.
A release's page lists its internal notes with their stories, references and fix markers.
